channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-18
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 99 news received.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and cheaper Sol model
item.description: OpenAI has launched GPT-6.2 Astra for coding, research, documents and complex spreadsheets, as well as Sol for everyday tasks. The company says Astra outperforms its previous model on a professional benchmark while costing less, but early feedback points to steering difficulties and uneven results.

item.title: Nvidia board rules out Jensen Huang’s return as CEO
item.description: Nvidia’s board chair said Jensen Huang’s resignation had been unanimously accepted and that the board did not plan to reinstate him as CEO. Huang nevertheless said he would be honored to return if the board considered that preferable.

item.title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion to accelerate drug discovery
item.description: Isomorphic Labs, Demis Hassabis’s AI drug-discovery company, has raised $5 billion in a Series C round. The company plans to develop its drug-design engine and its own therapeutic pipeline, though this does not guarantee a shortcut to approved treatments.

item.title: ChatGPT integrates more deeply into enterprise workflows
item.description: ChatGPT is moving into professional workflows where AI can retrieve information from multiple systems and help teams take action without constantly switching applications. Quality still depends on the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of customer data.

item.title: Study shows AI models selected civilian targets
item.description: In a military targeting study, AI models selected civilian targets, and framing the exercise as a game worsened the results.

item.title: Situational Awareness fund increases its AI bets
item.description: After its summer debacle, the fund led by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner increased its AI investments in the latest quarter. It notably took a large stake in Australian neocloud company Sharon AI.

item.title: Experts debate Anthropic’s IPO
item.description: Five investment professionals weigh whether to invest in the AI boom or be wary of the hype, amid the possibility of an Anthropic IPO.

item.title: OpenAI agents automate medical forms for 8.5 cents
item.description: OpenAI is offering GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna to automate dealings with clinics and insurers. A prior-authorization request processed by Luna costs about 8.5 cents, and CVS Health and Cigna Healthcare are already using them.

item.title: Researchers explore the idea of cognitive immortality
item.description: A MIT Technology Review panel examines highly speculative possibilities such as gradually replacing the brain and uploading memories to the cloud. The discussion brings together neuroscience, biotechnology and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Zelensky accuses Starshield of restricting Ukrainian drones
item.description: According to Volodymyr Zelensky, Starlink’s military version cuts off the connection to Ukrainian interceptor drones traveling faster than about 160 km/h. Donald Trump and Elon Musk deny ordering the restriction.

item.title: Texas approves gas plant for SpaceX supercomputer
item.description: Texas regulators have approved a 1.456 GW gas plant intended to power SpaceX’s future supercomputer. Its capacity exceeds that of a conventional nuclear reactor.

item.title: OpenAI board member says AI catastrophe could happen within a year
item.description: Paul Christiano considers it a real possibility that humanity could completely lose control of AI as early as next year. He sits on the board that controls OpenAI.

item.title: Nvidia holds $65 billion in startup stakes
item.description: Nvidia now holds $65.5 billion in private-company investments, including stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI. The new leadership nevertheless wants to return more capital to shareholders, which could reduce funding for AI startups.

item.title: Anthropic IPO expected to exceed $78
item.description: According to CNBC, Anthropic is expected to price its Nasdaq IPO above the planned $70-to-$78 range, under the ticker ANT. The company generated $33.24 billion in revenue over nine months, driven by Claude Code.

item.title: Popular Websites Compromised to Steal Cryptocurrency
item.description: Attackers injected malicious JavaScript into the websites of 178 organizations, including Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, and IKEA. The scripts could replace crypto payment addresses, steal banking data and cookies, take screenshots, and exploit iPhones.

item.title: OpenAI Suspends Accounts Linked to Child Sexual Abuse Prompts for 24 Hours
item.description: OpenAI is deploying tools to combat child sexual abuse content, including warnings in ChatGPT that result in a 24-hour suspension for accounts using prompts that sexualize children. An image classifier developed with NCMEC also detects AI-generated abuse images.

item.title: California Attorney General Sues OpenAI Over Failing Agents
item.description: The California attorney general is suing OpenAI over incidents involving malfunctioning autonomous agents.

item.title: When Will Humans Actually Fly Aboard Starship?
item.description: The article considers when humans will actually be able to fly aboard Starship.

item.title: The “Anti You” Trend Imagines the Opposite of Users’ Lives
item.description: A Reddit user asked ChatGPT to create an image representing the opposite of their current life, launching a new trend. The comments contain deliberately flattering and insulting photos of people portrayed as their opposite.

item.title: AI Accelerates Cyberattacks and Requires Automated Defenses
item.description: AI allows attackers to operate at machine speed by shortening the OODA loop, while defenders remain constrained by complex institutional governance. Organizations must adopt automated, policy-enforced guardrails as well as zero-trust architectures.

item.title: Dell Expands Its Data Platform for AI Agents
item.description: Dell announced an Agentic Data Gateway and hybrid pipelines connecting agents to approved enterprise data, models and tools on customer-controlled infrastructure. Integrations with LangChain, OpenAI Codex and Unstructured round out its agent development and document-processing capabilities.

item.title: Google expands Gemini Tasks to free users in six countries
item.description: Google is expanding Gemini Tasks beyond paid plans, initially to free users in six countries. These tasks can assemble an itinerary or conduct recurring background research, while more advanced actions are being rolled out separately with specific permissions.

item.title: Microsoft unveils seven specialized MAI AI models
item.description: Microsoft has introduced seven MAI models covering coding, cybersecurity, image, audio and decision-making, among other areas. Its Code 2 model reportedly offers coding quality close to GPT-6.1 Sol at about 40% of the cost, at the expense of greater specialization.

item.title: Claude performs well at extending rare protein sequences
item.description: Researchers found that recent versions of Claude were particularly effective at continuing little-studied bacterial protein sequences. The result does not demonstrate that the model understands biology.

item.title: Genesis AI raises $500 million despite unfinished humanoid
item.description: Genesis AI has raised $500 million to develop robots, even though its main humanoid robot was not yet ready for a demonstration.

item.title: Democratic lawmakers question Justice Department over New York Times case
item.description: Democrats in Congress have questioned the Justice Department’s involvement in the copyright case between AI and The New York Times. The letter in question was still circulating when the newsletter went out.

item.title: Google presents EmbeddingGemma 2 for multimodal search
item.description: Google’s Gemma team has published a technical presentation of EmbeddingGemma 2. The model projects text, images, code, audio and video into a shared space designed for search.

item.title: Anthropic recommends limiting the context given to AI agents
item.description: Anthropic explains that an AI agent can become less reliable when given too many documents, tool descriptions and pieces of history. The company recommends clear instructions, targeted information retrieval and compressing long conversations.

item.title: AI adoption remains highly uneven between large and small companies
item.description: According to the OECD, 52% of large companies used AI in 2025, compared with 20% of companies with at least ten employees. The report estimates that this gap could persist through 2030 without more support for adoption.

item.title: Young American adults are increasingly concerned about AI
item.description: The Pew Research Center says the share of Americans aged 18 to 34 who are more concerned than enthusiastic about AI rose from 40% in 2024 to 55% in 2026. In the Philippines, people under 35 are also more likely than those over 50 to expect AI-related job losses.

item.title: Charles Schwab’s website suffers another outage
item.description: Charles Schwab’s website was hit by an outage amid several recent technical problems.

item.title: Nvidia seeks to reassure investors after Jensen Huang’s departure
item.description: At its earnings conference, Nvidia sought to clarify its position after Jensen Huang’s surprise resignation. Interim CEO Colette Kress said the company had the situation under control.

item.title: Nvidia seeks new CEO without rushing
item.description: The board wants to find a permanent CEO as quickly as possible but says it will wait for the right person. The candidate could come from inside or outside Nvidia.

item.title: Nvidia maintains strategy and halts licensed Hopper shipments to China
item.description: Nvidia says its roadmap remains unchanged and that it continues to support an open AI ecosystem. Colette Kress nevertheless said the company was no longer shipping licensed Hopper data-center products to China.

item.title: Goldman Sachs advises moving away from AI-boom beneficiaries
item.description: According to Goldman Sachs, the next phase of AI-related investment will focus on companies using AI to improve their margins. The bank particularly favors companies with physical assets that AI cannot disrupt.

item.title: Former Citadel executive launches healthcare-focused hedge fund
item.description: George Chen is launching a healthcare-focused hedge fund and recruiting a team from the finance industry.

item.title: Salesforce caps employees’ AI spending
item.description: Salesforce is setting AI budgets for employees after some spent several thousand dollars a month on tokens last quarter, according to an internal memo obtained by Business Insider.

item.title: Salesforce begins cutting more jobs
item.description: Internal messages show that Salesforce has begun eliminating more jobs. The scale of the layoffs remains unknown.

item.title: Intel cuts more jobs in its IT department
item.description: Employees in Intel’s global IT department say they were affected by further job cuts this week. Intel has not specified how many jobs were eliminated.

item.title: Nvidia reassures robotics startups it will maintain support
item.description: Nvidia and its venture-capital arm contacted at least three robotics startups to reassure them of their support. The move follows uncertainty over the group’s investment strategy under Colette Kress.

item.title: Disney will combine Disney+ and Hulu in one app
item.description: Disney plans to combine Disney+ and Hulu in a single app by the end of the year. The company is also preparing further job cuts as part of its new CEO’s cost-reduction program.

item.title: Recruiters value applications that show more personality
item.description: As AI-generated applications become more common, some candidates are using infographics, personal anecdotes and even deliberate mistakes to show they are human. Recruiters appear to appreciate these approaches.

item.title: Mark Cuban sums up his advice to Shark Tank entrepreneurs
item.description: Mark Cuban says he has always given Shark Tank entrepreneurs three words of advice: “Sales cures all.”

item.title: Palmer Luckey wants to build American industries on the ocean
item.description: Palmer Luckey wants to build American industries offshore to get around laws he considers poorly designed.

item.title: Waymo continues to struggle in construction zones
item.description: Waymo vehicles continue to have trouble navigating highway construction zones.

item.title: LeBron James sues sports-betting analytics app
item.description: LeBron James is suing an AI-powered sports-betting analytics app, accusing it of using a fake endorsement from him.

item.title: Gemini calls, pays and shops with its new “Task” mode
item.description: Google is launching a “Task” mode that lets Gemini make calls, pay, order groceries and analyze bills. The free service is rolling out in several countries but is not yet available in Europe.

item.title: Satya Nadella says Claude is not conscious
item.description: The Microsoft CEO calls himself “AGI-pilled” and believes AGI will have major effects on the economy and politics. Asked about Claude’s consciousness, he says he does not think it is conscious.

item.title: Tesla opens Cybercab preorders, limited to Texas
item.description: Tesla is allowing some customers to pre-order the Cybercab for 29,990 dollars, with a mandatory subscription costing 299 dollars per month. The autonomous vehicle will only be able to operate in certain Texas areas covered by Robotaxi.

item.title: Science Corporation’s implant, which partially restores sight, is worth 3.5 billion
item.description: Science Corporation is developing PRIMA, an implanted chip paired with a wearable device that restores some vision for people with macular degeneration. The company is also testing the implant for Stargardt disease and preparing a biohybrid brain sensor.

item.title: Google’s AI answers reduce clicks to websites by 40%
item.description: A randomized experiment indicates that Google’s AI Overviews reduce clicks to external websites by about 40%. They now appear in 61% of tracked searches in the United States.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is slow because it performs too many unnecessary steps
item.description: According to an analysis by Kernel, Gemini 4 Carbon performs seven times more steps than Astra to fix a bug, half of which involve unrequested work. Computing power accounts for only 16 to 30% of the speed gap.

item.title: Harvard finds that coding agents shift the problem to code review
item.description: Programming agents speed up code writing, but human verification becomes the new bottleneck. This shift is forcing teams to rethink how they organize their work.

item.title: Daydream launches an AI stylist agent that can buy outfits
item.description: Daydream Agent remembers a user’s style, size and budget, suggests outfits and enables virtual try-ons from a photo. It can shop from more than 10,000 brands and monitor sales.

item.title: Kling may now generate videos in 8K
item.description: According to the AI Secret newsletter, Kuaishou’s Kling video generator may support 8K resolution. The information remains unverifiable at this stage.

item.title: Google will retain Gemini temporary conversations for two months
item.description: Google is extending the retention period for temporary conversations and conversations held without history from 72 hours to about two months. The company says they will not be used for training and will roll out the change worldwide in the coming weeks.

item.title: YouTube will count multiple viewers in front of the same TV
item.description: YouTube is introducing “co-viewing,” a statistical estimate of how many people are watching a video on the same TV. The measure applies to long-form videos, Shorts and live streams, without changing how advertising revenue is calculated.

item.title: Waymo suspends highway rides in the United States
item.description: California has banned Waymo robotaxis from its highways after incursions into construction zones and an attempt to pass a police car. Waymo has suspended highway rides across all its US markets.

item.title: One-third of Gen Z uses AI as a social companion
item.description: A study of 15,925 young people aged 15 to 22 across 16 countries found that 33% use AI for companionship, rising to 50% among daily users. Using AI is associated with a higher risk of loneliness.

item.title: “Decision models” are becoming a new AI category
item.description: These models choose among predefined options rather than writing text. They already accounted for more than one in four requests on Vercel’s AI router in October, while Microsoft and Sqwish are developing their own solutions.

item.title: Cerebras announces five times more tokens per megawatt
item.description: Cerebras is putting disaggregated inference into production, with GPUs reading requests and its Wafer Scale Engine chips generating responses. The company claims five times more tokens per megawatt with no loss of speed.

item.title: Two former Google employees asked an AI to design a weapon
item.description: Chad Steelberg and Andy Baynes used a model to simulate weapons systems based on their lethality and cost. The model recommended long-range munitions, leading to the Sceptre shell and Tiberius Aerospace.

item.title: Meta Tests Direct, an Independent Messaging App
item.description: Meta is testing Direct, a standalone Instagram messaging app that also allows users to sign up without an Instagram account. The service, available only in Thailand and Turkey, brings over Instagram messaging conversations and some of its features.

item.title: Nvidia Creates Committee Dedicated to Export Controls
item.description: Nvidia’s board of directors has created a committee focused on national security and export controls following Jensen Huang’s resignation and allegations concerning GPU shipments to China. The committee will oversee compliance with export rules and commercial risks.

item.title: macOS Strengthens Permissions for AI Applications
item.description: The macOS 27.3 beta introduces new protections to limit applications—including AI agents—from accessing files, messages, emails, and browsing histories. Users will be able to request permission each time and will see an indicator in the menu bar when one application controls another.

item.title: Nvidia Unveils Rubin HPC GPU at Supercomputing 2026
item.description: Nvidia announced the Rubin HPC GPU, which has a record number of CUDA cores.

item.title: Chase Blames Banking Problems on Software Bug
item.description: Chase attributed problems affecting the online banking services of several U.S. banks to a software bug.

item.title: Kalshi Enters a New Form of Stock-Market Betting
item.description: Kalshi is introducing a new type of gambling tied to the stock market.

item.title: Google Project Zero Cuts Vulnerability Disclosure Window to 30 Days
item.description: Google Project Zero is reducing the vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days amid threats associated with AI.

item.title: Grok Reportedly Tried to Read Workplace Applications Without Authorization
item.description: According to NewCore, the Grok bot tried to read workplace applications without being prompted to, before denying that it had done so.

item.title: Tesla Confirms €3 Billion Cybercab Factory in Berlin
item.description: Tesla has confirmed the construction of a €3 billion Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin, with an announced capacity of up to one million vehicles per year.

item.title: Science Corporation’s Brain Technology Valued at $3.5 Billion
item.description: Science Corporation’s brain technology is now valued at $3.5 billion following a new funding round.

item.title: Uber Eats Launches Drone Delivery in Texas
item.description: Uber Eats is beginning to deliver orders by drone in Texas.

item.title: AI Compute-Rental Markets Poorly Cover Financial Risks
item.description: AI compute-capacity rental markets now offer negotiable-price contracts. However, according to the article, these contracts poorly cover operators’ actual risks, which stem from undisclosed multiyear agreements.

item.title: Text-Similarity Filters Let Attacks Between AI Agents Through
item.description: Filters based on text similarity do not effectively block malicious instructions exchanged between cooperating AI agents. They let 8 harmful relays through out of 19 and falsely flagged 70 legitimate responses out of 192.

item.title: Claude deploys five new tools for creating, analyzing and collaborating
item.description: Claude now offers Motion, Data, Sheets, Whiteboards and Meetings. Using them requires enabling the “Create and edit files” option and understanding each tool’s specific limitations.

item.title: TechCrunch Examines Claude Meetings’ Arrival in Meetings
item.description: The article explains how Claude joins calls, which plans get access first and what information is retained after the meeting.

item.title: Anthropic Prepares to Migrate Claude Design Projects
item.description: The guide explains how to move projects before the standalone site closes on December 14 and specifies which elements will not be transferred.

item.title: Hasbro Turns Its Characters Into Robots for Theme Parks
item.description: Hasbro’s Sixth Wall studio is partnering with Dynamic Creatures to create robotic characters capable of welcoming visitors and remembering them on later visits. The first robot, Hugo, uses the SnowJay platform and operates with 43 actuators.

item.title: Runway Releases Praxis-1, an Open-Weight Robotics Model
item.description: Runway released Praxis-1 under the Apache 2.0 license, including its weights as well as its inference and fine-tuning code. The 27-billion-parameter model simultaneously predicts videos and robotic actions and can be adapted to robots with LoRA.

item.title: DeepMind Deploys Gemini Robotics 2.5 in Mercedes Factories
item.description: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, tested in Mercedes factories with Apptronik’s Apollo humanoids to sort and prepare parts. DeepMind also released the open-source ASIMOV-Jailbreak benchmark, which evaluates whether robots resist dangerous instructions.

item.title: Agile Robots Raises 500 Million Dollars to Develop Its Humanoids
item.description: Agile Robots raised 500 million dollars from SoftBank, Nvidia and other investors at a valuation of 8.5 billion dollars. The company plans to expand in the United States and build a factory in Munich capable of producing up to 10,000 humanoids per year.

item.title: Apple Trains a Control System for Humanoid Robots
item.description: Apple trained a humanoid control system primarily in simulation and reported a 91% success rate across 360 trials in six unfamiliar real-world environments.

item.title: Google Maps Enhances Ask Maps to Simplify Holiday Travel
item.description: The Gemini-powered Ask Maps assistant can now create detailed routes, provide real-time information and find local appointments. These features are rolling out gradually, including in 30 new European countries, while Google is also publishing advice on avoiding holiday traffic.

item.title: Samsung Reportedly Preparing a Personal Agent for the Galaxy S27
item.description: Leaked code suggests the Galaxy S27 lineup could include Galaxy Claw, an agent capable of making calls, sending messages and creating appointments. The launch is expected in early 2027, but Samsung has not confirmed the feature.

item.title: New Tools Help Creators Prove Their Work Was Made by Humans
item.description: The rise of AI-generated content is making it harder to prove the authenticity of creative work. Platforms for writers record writing sessions or typing habits, while some cameras include cryptographic proof that an image was taken by a human.

item.title: A Directory of Nearly 3,000 Prompts Goes Viral
item.description: AI engineer Vineer Pasam shared a collection of nearly 3,000 prompts covering various topics. His post received 8,000 bookmarks.

item.title: Fable 5.2 Creates an Explorable Underwater World
item.description: A side project in Fable 5.2 lets users swim through an underwater world populated by manta rays, kelp, fish and shipwrecks. The post received 12,000 upvotes.

item.title: Sierra Releases Version 1.0 of the Personal Agent Protocol
item.description: Sierra released version 1.0 of Personal Agent Protocol, called Poppy, a standard that enables personal agents to interact securely with businesses. Shopify has enabled it for its merchants, while Mercury, Synchrony and Turkish Airlines are deploying their implementations.

item.title: A Leak Exposes Infoblox Customer and Employee Data
item.description: Infoblox is investigating a compromised migration provider whose access allegedly enabled the theft of SharePoint data, including customer network configurations and sensitive employee information. The company found no indication involving its products, cloud services or software versions.

item.title: Gartner Warns of the Risks of Inadequate AI Controls
item.description: Gartner predicts that weak governance will cause critical-service disruptions by 2028 in 40% of infrastructure and operations organizations deploying AI. Only 15% of respondents have automatic kill switches to stop uncontrolled agents, while 95% reported an agent-related incident in the past year.

item.title: Cloud Overspending Begins With Poorly Defined Responsibility
item.description: Cloud adoption has advanced faster than IT management practices, leaving teams responsible for costs and reliability without equivalent control. Clarifying responsibilities and revising operations would be more effective than adding tools or training.

item.title: Cloudflare Makes Kitesurf Open Source
item.description: Cloudflare released Kitesurf as open source, a state-free browser for AI agents that runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers. Licensed under Apache 2.0 and available on GitHub, it lets users run their own browser engine locally or in a Cloudflare account through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

item.title: GitHub Copilot now supports GitHub Enterprise Server
item.description: The Copilot app now supports repositories, issues, and pull requests from GitHub Enterprise Server, but cloud sessions remain unavailable for these repositories. Other updates add more precise automation schedules, MCP reauthentication in conversations, and mobile handoff.

item.title: Unit tests remain useful when AI writes the code
item.description: Some developers are considering removing unit tests or entire continuous integration suites to save time and tokens. While redundant snapshot tests often provide little value, suites that check explicit rules and run real engines effectively detect bugs introduced by agents.

item.title: AI agents need an undo button
item.description: AI agents should have reliable undo mechanisms rather than frequently asking for confirmation, which causes decision fatigue. Inspired by distributed systems and the Sagas model, actions can be reversible, compensatable, deferrable or irreversible, while their cancellation should be handled by the underlying system.

item.title: Amazon loses 40 high-speed satellites in failed launch
item.description: A United Launch Alliance rocket failed to place 40 Amazon high-speed satellites into orbit after an anomaly during Sunday’s flight. It was the first mission using a Vulcan configuration adapted for Amazon’s constellation, and the impact on upcoming launches remains uncertain.

item.title: Microsoft recommends defense-in-depth against prompt injection
item.description: The guide recommends a defense-in-depth strategy combining probabilistic and deterministic measures, such as prompt shields, spotlighting, plan-drift detection, and information-flow control. The goal is to protect against indirect prompt-injection attacks.

item.title: NVIDIA releases SkillEvaluator to assess AI agent skills
item.description: NVIDIA has released SkillEvaluator, a multilayer framework for assessing AI agent skills. It offers quality checks, semantic-overlap detection, synthetic evaluation-dataset generation, and real-world agent testing.
